to_b->body.len = tmp - to_b->body.s;
tmp = parse_to_param(tmp, end, to_b, allow_comma_sep, &saved_status);
anchors.note: Source. After `get_hdr_field` has already dispatched the compact `T:` header body into the To parser, `parse_addr_spec` reaches the attacker-controlled semicolon in that body. This statement fixes the non-parameter body length and hands the parameter substring beginning at that semicolon, together with the unchanged `end` pointer for the whole 17-byte witness, into `parse_to_param`.

At the leading semicolon, `parse_to_param` starts a new general parameter record. The only vulnerability-relevant effect here is the state transition to `S_PARA_NAME`, which means the next attacker byte will be interpreted as the beginning of a parameter name.

The first byte after `;` is `0xff`. In state `S_PARA_NAME`, the default branch accepts that non-delimiter byte as the start of the parameter name by storing its address in `param->name.s` and switching the state machine to `PARA_NAME`.

When the parser reaches `=`, the one-byte name recorded in step 3 is closed and the state changes to `S_PARA_VALUE`. This state transition is what makes the following quote open a quoted value instead of being rejected as an unexpected character.

At the opening quote after `=`, the parser starts a quoted parameter value. It records the first byte after the quote as `param->value.s` and changes state to `PARA_VALUE_QUOTED`. The three following spaces in the witness do not change this state, so the parser remains in quoted-value mode until it reaches the final backslash.

Root cause. The witness ends with a backslash, so after the three quoted spaces from step 5 the loop reaches this branch with `tmp == end - 1` and `status == PARA_VALUE_QUOTED`. The vulnerable source checks only the parser state here; it does not test whether another byte exists before the next line inspects `tmp + 1`. The patch adds the missing `if(tmp+1>=end)` guard exactly at this point.

Sink. Because step 6 left `tmp` on the final backslash and there is no `tmp+1>=end` check, this expression dereferences the byte at `end`. ASan reports this exact read as a `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at line 228, 0 bytes past the 17-byte fuzz buffer.
